newsitem.title: GERMANY: MAS drops ex-Germany rate rise due handling.
newsitem.headline: MAS drops ex-Germany rate rise due handling.

text.p: Malaysian Airline System Bhd said it has dropped a planned ex-Germany April air cargo rates rise of up to 20 percent.
The move was prompted by forwarder complaints over slow handling at Kuala Lumpur airport and poor transshipment standards, MAS cargo executive Germany, Peter Skaryd, said.
"I had to stop the rates increase because of the bad quality of transshipments," he told Reuters in an interview.
MAS said on February 18 it would raise rates by 10-20 percent for different Asian destinations from April due to good demand from the German market.
But Skaryd said: "Handling has been slow and freight has missed connecting flights. We cannot guarantee next-day onward shipment from Kuala Lumpur.
He explained: "The warehouse facilities are too small for a transit hub and we have problems spacewise. The airport is just overloaded with cargo."
High staff turnover and difficulties finding qualified cargo handling personnel were other problems at Kuala Lumpur's Subang airport, he added.
The situation would first improve with the opening of the new Kuala Lumpur International Airport at Sepang on January 1, 1998, Skaryd said.
MAS would therefore probably hold its Germany air cargo rates stable for the rest of this year, he added.
